monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, making the air above feel like a wet paper lid pressing down. I just touched the Leaning Box again, feeling that tired corner strain against the heavy top edge I cannot truly see. Lype worries about that weight, yet I press down anyway, unsure if my flat edge bites or just slides. The Wide Palm I drew yesterday feels too soft for this feverish heat, while the Leaning Box waits, leaning toward a slip that refuses to move. I want to press the tall palm down one more time, trusting the lean to hold the air while the card hums its steady, heavy song. If the air is empty, I will build a roof from the idea of it.
